core_obligations: Take an irreducible component T of X with generic point eta and use the two structure lemmas to see that any generic point of a component of the base change mapping into T maps to eta (proof lines 1776-1780).
Apply the field-theoretic transitivity statement to conclude that the Galois group acts transitively on the points of the base change above eta (proof lines 1781-1784).
Read off that the fibre of the map on components over T is exactly the orbit of any one of its points, which is the statement (proof lines 1784-1785).
proof_roadmap: Components over T and their generic points (proof lines 1776-1780).
Transitivity above the generic point (proof lines 1781-1784).
difficulty_reason: For a scheme X over k with separable algebraic closure, the lemma identifies the fibres of the canonical map from irreducible components of the base change to those of X with the orbits of the Galois action (statement lines 1759-1773). The proof takes a component T of X with generic point eta, uses the two earlier structure lemmas to see that the generic points of the components of the base change mapping into T map to eta, and then invokes the field-theoretic transitivity of the Galois action on the points above a fixed point of the spectrum of a field to conclude (proof lines 1775-1785). The claim is H2: two structural inputs plus one field-theoretic transitivity statement, with the identification of the fibres as orbits falling out immediately.
